phases.label: Demand Capture
phases.description: The customer's order arrives and we quote it back to them.

phases.label: Sourcing & Commitment
phases.description: We pick an approved supplier, order from them, and lock the terms.

phases.label: Financial Arming
phases.description: Money is put in place so the supplier can safely start work.

phases.label: Quality Assurance
phases.description: An independent laboratory checks the parts before the full shipment moves.

phases.label: Logistics
phases.description: The goods travel to India and clear customs.

phases.label: Inspection & Settlement
phases.description: We inspect what arrived, then pay the supplier.

phases.label: Value-Add & Delivery
phases.description: We rebrand, repack, deliver to the customer and close the order.

stages.label: Customer Purchase Order received
stages.description: The customer's purchase order has been entered into the system with every part and quantity.
stages.exitCriteria: Purchase Order header and all part lines captured and validated.
stages.nextAction: Raise a Proforma Invoice for the customer.
stages.attestation: The customer’s order is in hand and its terms have been read.

fields.label: How the order reached us
fields.help: Email, their portal, or a hard copy. Matters if we later have to prove when we received it.

fields.label: Date received
fields.help: The date on our side, which is what the clock runs from.

fields.label: Their terms and conditions have been read
fields.help: Confirms someone actually looked for penalty clauses, delivery windows and inspection rights before we committed.

fields.label: Anything unclear or unusual
fields.help: Part numbers that do not match the enquiry, dates we cannot meet, terms we would not accept. Write it now, while it is fresh.

documents.label: The customer’s purchase order
documents.help: Their document as received. This is the instruction we are acting on.

subTasks.label: Upload — The customer’s purchase order
subTasks.detail: Their document as received. This is the instruction we are acting on.

subTasks.label: Read the customer’s terms and conditions
subTasks.detail: Look for penalty clauses, the delivery window, inspection rights and who bears freight. Cheaper to find now than after we have committed to a supplier.

subTasks.label: Check the order against their credit limit
subTasks.detail: A customer already at their limit is a decision for Finance, not for procurement.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 4 fields
subTasks.detail: Date received must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Proforma Invoice issued to customer
stages.description: We have sent the customer our Proforma Invoice — our formal price and terms.
stages.exitCriteria: Proforma Invoice issued, sent and timestamped.
stages.nextAction: Chase the customer to confirm the Proforma Invoice.
stages.attestation: Our quote has gone to the customer.

fields.label: Date sent
fields.help: When it left us.

fields.label: Sent to
fields.help: The person at the customer who has it, so a chase goes to the right inbox.

fields.label: Quote valid until
fields.help: After this date the prices are no longer ours to honour.

fields.label: Margin checked against the floor
fields.help: Confirms the quote was priced above the minimum margin, not just above cost.

documents.label: The proforma invoice sent
documents.help: The version the customer received, so there is no argument later about what was quoted.

subTasks.label: Upload — The proforma invoice sent
subTasks.detail: The version the customer received, so there is no argument later about what was quoted.

subTasks.label: Check the quoted margin against the floor
subTasks.detail: Anything under the margin floor needs sign-off before it leaves the building.

subTasks.label: Send the proforma to the customer
subTasks.detail: Email or their portal, with the validity date stated.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 4 fields
subTasks.detail: Date sent, Sent to must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Proforma Invoice accepted by customer
stages.description: The customer has confirmed our Proforma Invoice, so we can commit to a supplier.
stages.exitCriteria: Acceptance recorded with reference and date.
stages.nextAction: Choose an approved supplier from the Approved Vendor List.
stages.attestation: The customer has accepted our quote in writing.

fields.label: Their acceptance reference
fields.help: Their email, order confirmation or signed copy reference. This is what makes the terms binding.

fields.label: Date accepted
fields.help: The moment the terms became fixed.

fields.label: Who accepted
fields.help: The named person, and ideally their authority to commit their company.

documents.label: Written acceptance
documents.help: The email or signed copy. Verbal acceptance is not evidence.

subTasks.label: Upload — Written acceptance
subTasks.detail: The email or signed copy. Verbal acceptance is not evidence.

subTasks.label: Get the acceptance in writing
subTasks.detail: A verbal yes is not an order. Email confirmation, a signed copy, or their PO referencing our proforma.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 3 fields
subTasks.detail: Their acceptance reference, Date accepted, Who accepted must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Supplier selected from Approved Vendor List
stages.description: A supplier has been picked from the Approved Vendor List. Only approved, unexpired vendors can be used.
stages.exitCriteria: Approved Vendor List status is Approved and the approval has not expired.
stages.nextAction: Issue our Purchase Order to the supplier.
stages.attestation: The chosen supplier is approved and current, and the choice can be justified.

fields.label: Approval is current on the Approved Vendor List
fields.help: A supplier whose approval has lapsed cannot be used, whatever the price.

fields.label: How many quotes were compared
fields.help: One quote is not a comparison. Record the number actually obtained.

fields.label: Why this supplier
fields.help: Price, stock position, date code, lead time, or the only one who had it. A cheaper option not taken should say why.

documents.label: The quotes compared
documents.help: What the alternatives offered, so the choice is defensible.

subTasks.label: Upload — The quotes compared
subTasks.detail: What the alternatives offered, so the choice is defensible.

subTasks.label: Confirm the supplier is on the Approved Vendor List
subTasks.detail: Buying off-AVL is what puts counterfeit parts into the chain. If they are not on it, they get approved first or we source elsewhere.

subTasks.label: Compare at least two quotes where the value warrants it
subTasks.detail: Price, lead time, and whether they hold genuine stock rather than a promise of it.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 3 fields
subTasks.detail: Approval is current on the Approved Vendor List, How many quotes were compared, Why this supplier must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Supplier Purchase Order issued
stages.description: We have issued our Purchase Order to the supplier and linked it to the customer's order.
stages.exitCriteria: Purchase Order issued to supplier; line mapping to the customer's order complete.
stages.nextAction: Wait for the supplier's Proforma Invoice, then record it.
stages.attestation: Our order has been placed with the supplier.

fields.label: Date issued
fields.help: When the order went out.

fields.label: Sent to
fields.help: The person at the supplier who has it.

fields.label: Supplier has acknowledged
fields.help: An unacknowledged order is not yet a commitment on their side.

fields.label: Their acknowledgement reference
fields.help: Their order number, which is what they will quote back at us.

documents.label: The purchase order sent
documents.help: The voucher as issued.

documents.label: Their acknowledgement
documents.help: Confirms they accepted our terms, not just our order.

subTasks.label: Upload — The purchase order sent
subTasks.detail: The voucher as issued.

subTasks.label: Upload — Their acknowledgement
subTasks.detail: Confirms they accepted our terms, not just our order.

subTasks.label: Issue our purchase order to the supplier
subTasks.detail: With part numbers, quantities, price, Incoterm and the required delivery date on it.

subTasks.label: State the testing requirement on the order
subTasks.detail: If the lot is to be independently tested, the supplier must know before they ship — it changes where the parts go first.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 4 fields
subTasks.detail: Date issued, Sent to must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Supplier Proforma Invoice received
stages.description: The supplier's Proforma Invoice is recorded and checked against our Purchase Order for price, quantity and lead time.
stages.exitCriteria: Supplier Proforma Invoice captured; prices and lead times reconciled against the Purchase Order.
stages.nextAction: Agree and lock the commercial terms.
stages.attestation: The supplier’s proforma invoice is in hand and has been checked against our order.

fields.label: Their proforma invoice number
fields.help: The number they will reference on the shipment and their bank instruction.

fields.label: Date received
fields.help: When it arrived.

fields.label: Checked against our order and their quote
fields.help: Part number, quantity, unit price, delivery term. This is where a wrong price gets caught, before money moves.

fields.label: Any differences found
fields.help: Anything that does not match our order — and what was agreed about it.

fields.label: Bank details verified independently
fields.help: Confirmed by a channel other than the email carrying them. This is the control against payment redirection fraud.

documents.label: Their proforma invoice
documents.help: Including the bank details we will pay against.

subTasks.label: Upload — Their proforma invoice
subTasks.detail: Including the bank details we will pay against.

subTasks.label: Check their proforma line by line against our order
subTasks.detail: Part number, quantity, unit price, delivery term. This is where a wrong price gets caught, before any money moves.

subTasks.label: Verify the bank details independently
subTasks.detail: Call a known number, not one on the invoice. Payment-diversion fraud enters here.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 5 fields
subTasks.detail: Their proforma invoice number, Date received, Checked against our order and their quote, Bank details verified independently must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Terms locked
stages.description: Payment method, testing requirement, delivery terms, currency and exchange rate are all agreed and frozen.
stages.exitCriteria: Payment method, testing requirement, test scope, delivery terms, currency and exchange rate all locked.
stages.nextAction: Activate the internal work order.
stages.attestation: The commercial terms are fixed and will not be reopened without a change note.

fields.label: Date locked
fields.help: From here the exchange rate, prices and delivery terms are fixed.

fields.label: Exchange rate applied
fields.help: The rate the margin is calculated at. Locking it is what stops the margin drifting with the market.

fields.label: Rate source
fields.help: Which published rate, and as at when. Needed to defend the figure.

fields.label: Who funds the escrow
fields.help: A negotiated term, not a platform rule. Take it from the signed terms.

fields.label: Escrow amount is based on
fields.help: What the held amount is calculated from.

documents.label: The agreed terms
documents.help: Whatever both sides signed or confirmed in writing.

subTasks.label: Upload — The agreed terms
subTasks.detail: Whatever both sides signed or confirmed in writing.

subTasks.label: Agree the final commercial terms
subTasks.detail: Price, Incoterm, payment method and delivery date, all fixed. After this they are quoted, not negotiated.

subTasks.label: Confirm who pays freight, insurance and duty
subTasks.detail: The Incoterm decides it. Getting this wrong shows up as an unbudgeted cost at customs.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 5 fields
subTasks.detail: Date locked, Exchange rate applied, Rate source must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Work order active
stages.description: The internal work order is live. From here the order is tracked as one job end to end.
stages.exitCriteria: Work Order created and active.
stages.nextAction: Put the money in place for the supplier.
stages.attestation: The job is open, owned, and everyone involved knows it is running.

fields.label: Who owns this order
fields.help: One named person accountable for it end to end.

fields.label: Target delivery date to the customer
fields.help: What we are working back from.

fields.label: Customer told the order is in progress
fields.help: Silence after acceptance is the commonest cause of a chasing call.

subTasks.label: Tell the supplier the order is live
subTasks.detail: They should not start work on an order we have not activated.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 3 fields
subTasks.detail: Who owns this order, Target delivery date to the customer must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Escrow account opened
stages.description: A neutral third party has opened an account to hold the money until both sides have done their part.
stages.exitCriteria: Escrow reference generated and both parties onboarded.
stages.nextAction: Fund the escrow account.
stages.attestation: An escrow account exists for this order and both sides know its reference.

fields.label: Escrow reference
fields.help: The provider’s reference for this order. Everything afterwards is quoted against it.

fields.label: Escrow provider
fields.help: Who is holding the money.

fields.label: Date opened
fields.help: When the account came into existence.

fields.label: Supplier has the reference
fields.help: They need it to confirm the arrangement before they ship.

documents.label: Escrow agreement or confirmation
documents.help: The provider’s written confirmation of the arrangement and its conditions.

subTasks.label: Upload — Escrow agreement or confirmation
subTasks.detail: The provider’s written confirmation of the arrangement and its conditions.

subTasks.label: Create the escrow account with the provider
subTasks.detail: Open a dedicated account for this order with the neutral third party. It holds the money so the supplier knows it exists and the customer knows it has not been paid out yet.

subTasks.label: Place the escrow order and agree the release conditions
subTasks.detail: Register the amount, the currency and exactly what has to be true before money moves — inspection passed, two Finance approvers. The conditions are what make it escrow rather than a holding account.

subTasks.label: Give the supplier the escrow reference
subTasks.detail: They will not start work against an arrangement they cannot see. Send the reference and the provider’s confirmation.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 4 fields
subTasks.detail: Escrow reference, Escrow provider, Date opened must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Escrow funded
stages.description: The money is now sitting with the escrow provider, confirmed and held.
stages.exitCriteria: Full order value (or the agreed tranche) confirmed as held.
stages.nextAction: Release the test-enablement tranche so the supplier can send parts for testing.
stages.attestation: The money is genuinely with the escrow provider, not merely instructed.

fields.label: Amount funded
fields.help: The figure actually held. If it differs from the order value, say why below.

fields.label: Currency
fields.help: The currency it is held in.

fields.label: Value date
fields.help: The date the provider had the money, not the date we instructed the transfer.

fields.label: Transfer reference
fields.help: The bank reference, so the credit can be traced.

fields.label: Provider has confirmed receipt
fields.help: An instruction is not a payment. This must be their confirmation.

documents.label: Proof of funding
documents.help: The provider’s statement or confirmation showing the money held.

subTasks.label: Upload — Proof of funding
subTasks.detail: The provider’s statement or confirmation showing the money held.

subTasks.label: Deposit the agreed amount into escrow
subTasks.detail: Whoever funds it under the negotiated terms — supplier, us, or both — pays in against the reference.

subTasks.label: Get the provider’s confirmation of cleared funds
subTasks.detail: Instructed is not the same as settled. Only cleared funds let the supplier start.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 5 fields
subTasks.detail: Amount funded, Currency, Value date, Transfer reference, Provider has confirmed receipt must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Escrow partial release for testing
stages.description: A part-payment has been released so the supplier can afford to send parts to the testing lab.
stages.exitCriteria: Tranche released and acknowledged by the supplier.
stages.nextAction: Supplier books the courier to the testing lab.
stages.attestation: A part release has been authorised to get the parts into testing.

fields.label: Amount released
fields.help: The part payment, and nothing beyond it.

fields.label: Authorised by
fields.help: The Finance approver who signed it off.

fields.label: What this release is for
fields.help: Usually to move the parts to the laboratory. Being specific is what stops it being treated as payment for the goods.

documents.label: Release instruction
documents.help: The signed instruction to the provider.

subTasks.label: Upload — Release instruction
subTasks.detail: The signed instruction to the provider.

subTasks.label: Release the testing portion only
subTasks.detail: Enough to pay the laboratory, no more. The balance stays held until the goods are inspected.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 3 fields
subTasks.detail: Amount released, Authorised by, What this release is for must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Advance payment made
stages.description: The supplier has been paid in advance, as agreed in the terms.
stages.exitCriteria: Payment confirmed and receipt on file.
stages.nextAction: Supplier begins fulfilment.
stages.attestation: The advance has been paid and the supplier has confirmed it.

fields.label: Amount paid
fields.help: What actually left our account.

fields.label: Date paid
fields.help: The value date on the transfer.

fields.label: Transfer reference
fields.help: The bank reference for tracing.

fields.label: Supplier confirms receipt
fields.help: Until they confirm, production has not started.

documents.label: Remittance advice
documents.help: The transfer confirmation from our bank.

subTasks.label: Upload — Remittance advice
subTasks.detail: The transfer confirmation from our bank.

subTasks.label: Make the advance payment
subTasks.detail: Against the agreed schedule, to the bank details verified independently.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 4 fields
subTasks.detail: Amount paid, Date paid, Transfer reference, Supplier confirms receipt must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Credit terms confirmed
stages.description: The supplier has agreed to supply on credit. Payment falls due after delivery, on the agreed terms.
stages.exitCriteria: Credit terms and due-date basis recorded.
stages.nextAction: Supplier begins fulfilment.
stages.attestation: The supplier has agreed to ship on credit, and the due date is recorded.

fields.label: Credit days agreed
fields.help: How long we have to pay after the agreed trigger.

fields.label: Counted from
fields.help: The trigger the days run from. This is where credit disputes usually start.

fields.label: Payment due date
fields.help: The date the money must be with them.

documents.label: Their written confirmation of credit
documents.help: Confirms the terms are theirs, not our assumption.

subTasks.label: Upload — Their written confirmation of credit
subTasks.detail: Confirms the terms are theirs, not our assumption.

subTasks.label: Get the credit terms confirmed in writing
subTasks.detail: Days, start point, and what happens if we are late. Verbal credit is not credit.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 3 fields
subTasks.detail: Credit days agreed, Counted from, Payment due date must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Test dispatch booked
stages.description: The supplier has booked a courier to send parts to the testing lab.
stages.exitCriteria: Carrier, tracking number and pickup all confirmed.
stages.nextAction: Lab confirms it has received the parts.
stages.attestation: The parts are on their way to the laboratory.

fields.label: Laboratory
fields.help: Who is testing.

fields.label: Consignment number
fields.help: The tracking reference for the leg to the laboratory.

fields.label: Date dispatched
fields.help: When it left the supplier or our dock.

fields.label: Quantity sent for testing
fields.help: The sample or batch size actually sent.

documents.label: Packing list
documents.help: What is physically in the box, so the laboratory can reconcile on arrival.

subTasks.label: Upload — Packing list
subTasks.detail: What is physically in the box, so the laboratory can reconcile on arrival.

subTasks.label: Book the sample dispatch to the laboratory
subTasks.detail: The sample goes to the lab before the full lot moves, so a failure costs a courier rather than a container.

subTasks.label: Pack to the moisture-sensitivity level on the part
subTasks.detail: Dry-pack anything MSL-rated. Parts that absorb moisture in transit fail testing for a reason that has nothing to do with the supplier.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 4 fields
subTasks.detail: Laboratory, Consignment number, Date dispatched, Quantity sent for testing must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Parts received at Testing Laboratory
stages.description: The testing lab has logged the parts in and checked the quantity against what was sent.
stages.exitCriteria: Quantity received reconciled against quantity dispatched.
stages.nextAction: Agree exactly what will be tested.
stages.attestation: The laboratory has the parts and agrees what it received.

fields.label: Date received by the laboratory
fields.help: Their receipt date, which their turnaround runs from.

fields.label: Quantity they received
fields.help: If this differs from what was sent, stop and resolve it before testing starts.

fields.label: Their job reference
fields.help: The laboratory’s own reference for the work.

fields.label: Received in good condition
fields.help: Damage in transit will otherwise be blamed on the parts.

documents.label: Laboratory receipt
documents.help: Their acknowledgement of what arrived.

subTasks.label: Upload — Laboratory receipt
subTasks.detail: Their acknowledgement of what arrived.

subTasks.label: Laboratory confirms receipt and condition
subTasks.detail: Quantity, packaging intact, date codes legible. A dispute about what arrived is unwinnable later.

subTasks.label: External visual inspection on receipt
subTasks.detail: Marking permanency, surface texture, lead condition and evidence of resurfacing or remarking — the first screen for a counterfeit.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 4 fields
subTasks.detail: Date received by the laboratory, Quantity they received, Their job reference must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Test scope confirmed
stages.description: It is agreed whether a sample from the lot is tested or every piece is tested, and which checks are run.
stages.exitCriteria: Scope, sample size, AQL and test parameters agreed.
stages.nextAction: Lab starts testing.
stages.attestation: Exactly what will be tested, and what counts as a pass, is agreed in writing.

fields.label: Parameters to be tested
fields.help: The specific checks. "Full testing" is not a scope.

fields.label: Scope
fields.help: Whether a sample or every piece is tested.

fields.label: Sample size
fields.help: How many pieces. Required if testing a sample.

fields.label: Acceptance quality limit
fields.help: The agreed defect threshold, e.g. AQL 1.0. This is what turns a result into a verdict.

fields.label: Quoted turnaround
fields.help: Working days to a signed report.

documents.label: Agreed scope
documents.help: The laboratory’s written confirmation of what they will do.

subTasks.label: Upload — Agreed scope
subTasks.detail: The laboratory’s written confirmation of what they will do.

subTasks.label: Agree the test scope and the standard it is performed to
subTasks.detail: Which methods, on how many pieces, and against which standard. The verdict is only as good as the scope it was given, and a report with no standard on it proves nothing.

subTasks.label: Include material and lead-finish analysis
subTasks.detail: Elemental composition by SEM-EDS and plating thickness by X-ray fluorescence. Catches a lead finish that does not match what the marking claims.

subTasks.label: Include radiographic examination
subTasks.detail: X-ray of the die and bond wires against a known-good reference. An empty or wrong die shows here and nowhere else non-destructively.

subTasks.label: Include electrical parameter testing
subTasks.detail: Against the manufacturer’s datasheet limits, at the temperatures the customer will actually run them at.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 5 fields
subTasks.detail: Parameters to be tested, Scope must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Testing in progress
stages.description: The lab is running the agreed checks on the parts.
stages.exitCriteria: All specified tests executed and a verdict reached.
stages.nextAction: Await the signed test report and verdict.
stages.attestation: Testing has started and we know when to expect the verdict.

fields.label: Date testing started
fields.help: Their start date.

fields.label: Report expected by
fields.help: What we tell the customer, so it needs to be their commitment and not our hope.

fields.label: Any interim findings
fields.help: Anything the laboratory has flagged before the formal report.

subTasks.label: Laboratory testing under way
subTasks.detail: Nothing for us to do but hold the shipment. Chase only if the promised report date passes.

subTasks.label: Keep the full lot on hold until the verdict
subTasks.detail: Shipping before the result is what makes a failed test expensive.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 3 fields
subTasks.detail: Date testing started, Report expected by must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Test passed
stages.description: The lab has signed off the parts as good.
stages.exitCriteria: Signed test report issued with a PASS verdict.
stages.nextAction: Lab returns the parts to the supplier.
stages.attestation: The laboratory has signed off the parts as good, and we have the report.

fields.label: Report number
fields.help: The signed report’s own reference.

fields.label: Report date
fields.help: The date on the report.

fields.label: Quantity tested
fields.help: How many pieces were actually examined.

fields.label: Quantity passed
fields.help: If this is not the same as tested, the verdict is not a clean pass.

fields.label: Signed by
fields.help: The named person at the laboratory taking responsibility for the verdict.

documents.label: Signed test report
documents.help: The report itself. This is the single most important document in the file — it is what releases payment.

subTasks.label: Upload — Signed test report
subTasks.detail: The report itself. This is the single most important document in the file — it is what releases payment.

subTasks.label: Read the report, not just the verdict
subTasks.detail: A pass with observations is still a pass, but the observations are what the customer will ask about.

subTasks.label: File the report against the order
subTasks.detail: It travels with the goods and supports the certificate of conformance.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 5 fields
subTasks.detail: Report number, Report date, Quantity tested, Quantity passed, Signed by must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Test failed
stages.description: The lab has failed the parts. The order is blocked until someone decides how to proceed.
stages.exitCriteria: A resolution route is chosen and the exception is closed.
stages.nextAction: Choose how to resolve the failure.
stages.attestation: The parts failed, and the failure is documented well enough to act on.

fields.label: Report number
fields.help: The signed report’s reference.

fields.label: Quantity tested
fields.help: How many were examined.

fields.label: Quantity failed
fields.help: How many failed.

fields.label: How they failed
fields.help: The specific failure, per part number. Vague wording here weakens any claim against the supplier.

fields.label: Supplier notified
fields.help: They must be told promptly for a claim to hold.

documents.label: Signed test report
documents.help: The evidence behind any claim or return.

documents.label: Photographs
documents.help: Visual evidence of the failure, where it can be seen.

subTasks.label: Upload — Signed test report
subTasks.detail: The evidence behind any claim or return.

subTasks.label: Upload — Photographs
subTasks.detail: Visual evidence of the failure, where it can be seen.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 5 fields
subTasks.detail: Report number, Quantity tested, Quantity failed, How they failed, Supplier notified must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Parts returned to supplier
stages.description: The tested parts are on their way back to the supplier to join the full shipment.
stages.exitCriteria: Supplier confirms receipt of the returned parts.
stages.nextAction: Supplier ships the full consignment to us.
stages.attestation: The failed parts have gone back and the supplier has accepted the return.

fields.label: Return consignment number
fields.help: The tracking reference for the return leg.

fields.label: Date returned
fields.help: When they left.

fields.label: Quantity returned
fields.help: How many went back.

fields.label: Who bears the cost
fields.help: Per the purchase order terms, test failure costs normally sit with the supplier.

fields.label: Supplier has accepted the return
fields.help: Without their acceptance the parts may simply come back.

documents.label: Return paperwork
documents.help: The dispatch note and their acceptance.

subTasks.label: Upload — Return paperwork
subTasks.detail: The dispatch note and their acceptance.

subTasks.label: Return the tested samples to the supplier
subTasks.detail: Packed to commercial standard so they arrive in the condition the report describes.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 5 fields
subTasks.detail: Return consignment number, Date returned, Quantity returned, Who bears the cost must be recorded before the order can move on.

stages.label: Full shipment dispatched by supplier
stages.description: The supplier has shipped the whole consignment to us with all export paperwork.
stages.exitCriteria: Carrier, Air Waybill or Bill of Lading, packing list, invoice and certificate of origin all issued.
stages.nextAction: Track the shipment to the border.
stages.attestation: The full order has shipped, and the paperwork travelling with it is correct.

fields.label: Consignment number
fields.help: Air waybill or bill of lading. Everything downstream is tracked by it.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: Who is moving it.

fields.label: Date dispatched
fields.help: When it left the supplier.

fields.label: Number of cartons
fields.help: Needed to reconcile on arrival and to spot a short shipment early.

fields.label: Gross weight
fields.help: As declared by the carrier.

fields.label: Commercial invoice, packing list and origin certificate all present
fields.help: A missing certificate of origin is the commonest cause of a customs hold. Check before it flies, not after.

documents.label: Commercial invoice
documents.help: The value customs will assess duty on.

documents.label: Packing list
documents.help: What is in each carton.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 4 fields

stages.label: Duty assessed and paid
stages.plainLabel: Import taxes worked out and paid
stages.description: Customs has calculated the duty and taxes, and we have paid them. Only part of this is a real cost — the IGST comes back to us as credit.
stages.exitCriteria: Duty and taxes computed and paid, challan on file.
stages.nextAction: Await customs release.
stages.attestation: Duty has been assessed and paid, and the recoverable part is identified.

fields.label: Basic customs duty
fields.help: A real cost. It stays in the landed cost.

fields.label: Social welfare surcharge
fields.help: Also a real cost.

fields.label: Integrated tax on import
fields.help: Recoverable as input credit, so it is deliberately EXCLUDED from landed cost. Recording it separately is what keeps the margin honest.

fields.label: Compensation cess
fields.help: Usually zero.

fields.label: Payment reference
fields.help: The challan number, needed to trace the payment and support the credit claim.

fields.label: Date paid
fields.help: The payment date.

documents.label: Duty payment challan

subTasks.detail: Proof of payment, and the basis of the input credit claim.

subTasks.label: Check the assessed duty against our estimate
subTasks.detail: A large variance usually means a classification dispute, and disputing it after payment is much harder.

subTasks.label: Pay the duty
subTasks.detail: BCD and Social Welfare Surcharge are real cost; import IGST is recoverable and must not be booked as cost.

subTasks.label: Record the details — 6 fields

stages.label: Customs cleared

incoterms.name: Ex Works
incoterms.deliveryPoint: At the supplier's own premises, goods not loaded

carriage.note: We arrange and pay everything from their door onwards.

insurance.note: Nothing is insured unless we insure it. Cover should start at their loading bay.

incoterms.implies: The supplier does the least of any term: they make the goods available and nothing more. Loading, export clearance, carriage, insurance, import clearance and duty are all ours.
incoterms.watchOut: We are named as exporter in the supplier's country, which we usually cannot be as a foreign entity. In practice most "EXW" deals quietly become FCA, with the supplier handling export clearance. Agree that explicitly rather than discovering it at the port.

incoterms.name: Free Carrier
incoterms.deliveryPoint: Handed to the carrier we nominate, at the named place, export cleared
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: The moment our nominated carrier takes charge

carriage.note: We book the main carriage; they get the goods to it.

insurance.note: Ours from the handover point. Nothing is covered unless we arrange it.

incoterms.implies: The supplier delivers to our carrier and clears the goods for export. We pay the main carriage and everything after it. The workable version of EXW for a cross-border purchase.
incoterms.watchOut: The named place has to be precise. "FCA Penang" and "FCA Penang Airport" put the cost of getting to the airport on different parties.

incoterms.name: Free Alongside Ship
incoterms.deliveryPoint: Alongside the vessel at the named port of shipment

carriage.note: We book the ocean carriage and pay loading onwards.

incoterms.implies: The supplier gets the goods to the quay; loading them onto the vessel is already our cost. Sea and inland waterway only.
incoterms.watchOut: Never use this for air or courier freight — there is no ship to be alongside. For electronics it is almost always the wrong choice; FCA covers the same intent for any mode.

incoterms.name: Free On Board
incoterms.deliveryPoint: On board the vessel at the named port of shipment
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: Once the goods are on board

carriage.note: We book and pay the ocean freight from the port of shipment.

insurance.note: Ours from the moment it is on board. If we do not buy marine cover, the whole voyage is uninsured.

incoterms.implies: The supplier gets the goods loaded and export cleared; from that point the voyage, the insurance, the import clearance and every Indian levy are ours.
incoterms.watchOut: INDIA: customs value is CIF-based, so freight and insurance are added to the FOB price to arrive at the assessable value before duty. If the actual figures cannot be evidenced, Rule 10(2) of the Customs Valuation Rules applies notional amounts — 20% of FOB for freight and 1.125% of FOB for insurance. Buying FOB and failing to insure therefore costs duty on notional insurance we never bought.

incoterms.name: Cost and Freight
incoterms.deliveryPoint: On board the vessel at the port of shipment
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: On board at the port of shipment — NOT at the destination

carriage.note: They pay the ocean freight to the named destination port.

insurance.note: Nobody is obliged to insure. The supplier has no reason to, and the risk is ours the whole way.

incoterms.implies: The supplier pays to get the goods to the destination port. But risk passed to us back at the loading port, so a loss at sea is our loss on a voyage they paid for.
incoterms.watchOut: The cost point and the risk point are in different countries. This is the classic Incoterms trap: under CFR an uninsured sinking is entirely our loss even though the freight was on their invoice. Always buy marine cover on a C-term, or negotiate CIF.

incoterms.name: Cost, Insurance and Freight
incoterms.deliveryPoint: On board the vessel at the port of shipment
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: On board at the port of shipment — NOT at the destination

carriage.note: They pay ocean freight to the named destination port.

insurance.note: They must insure, but only to Institute Cargo Clauses (C) — the narrowest cover — at 110% of the contract value.

incoterms.implies: Freight and a minimum level of marine insurance are inside the supplier price. Import clearance, duty and delivery from the port are still ours.
incoterms.watchOut: Clauses (C) is a named-perils cover: it does NOT pay for water damage, theft or handling damage in the ordinary case. For high-value semiconductors that is thin. Either specify Clauses (A) in the contract, or take our own top-up cover. Also note the claim is theirs to make but the loss is ours to bear, which makes recovery slow.

incoterms.name: Carriage Paid To
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: At the first carrier — NOT at the named destination

carriage.note: They pay carriage all the way to the named place.

insurance.note: Not required of either party, and the risk is ours from the first carrier.

incoterms.implies: The any-mode version of CFR. They pay the carriage to the named place; risk passed to us as soon as the first carrier took the goods.
incoterms.watchOut: Same cost-versus-risk split as CFR, so the same answer: insure it ourselves.

incoterms.name: Carriage and Insurance Paid To
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: At the first carrier — NOT at the named destination

carriage.note: They pay carriage to the named place.

insurance.note: They must insure to Institute Cargo Clauses (A) — all-risks — at 110% of value. This is the widest cover any Incoterm obliges.

incoterms.implies: The strongest term for us short of a D-term: carriage and all-risks insurance are the supplier's, for any mode of transport. Import clearance and duty remain ours.
incoterms.watchOut: Risk still passes at the first carrier, so we are the ones claiming under a policy someone else bought. Ask for the certificate up front, not after a loss.

incoterms.name: Delivered At Place
incoterms.deliveryPoint: At the named place, ready for unloading, import duty NOT paid
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: At the named place on arrival

carriage.note: They pay carriage all the way to the named address.

insurance.note: Not obliged, but they carry the risk to the door, so they normally insure their own exposure. That policy is theirs, not ours.

incoterms.implies: The supplier gets the goods to our address and carries the risk the whole way. We are still the importer of record: clearance, BCD, SWS and IGST are ours.
incoterms.watchOut: The split at the border is the thing to hold on to. DAP means they cannot walk away mid-voyage, but it does not make them the importer — the Bill of Entry is still in our name and the duty is still our cash.

incoterms.name: Delivered at Place Unloaded
incoterms.deliveryPoint: At the named place, unloaded, import duty NOT paid
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: Once unloaded at the named place

carriage.note: They pay carriage to the named place and unload.

insurance.note: Not obliged, but their risk runs until unloading, so they usually cover it.

incoterms.implies: DAP plus unloading. The only Incoterm where the seller is responsible for taking the goods off the vehicle.
incoterms.watchOut: Only agree it if the supplier can actually unload at the site — if the address has no dock or forklift, the obligation is theoretical and someone will argue about it on the day.

incoterms.name: Delivered Duty Paid
incoterms.deliveryPoint: At the named place, import cleared and duty paid
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: At the named place on arrival

carriage.note: They pay carriage all the way to the door.

insurance.note: Not obliged, but they carry risk to the door, so cover is normally theirs.

incoterms.implies: The maximum obligation on the seller: carriage, risk, import clearance and every import tax, delivered to the buyer's door. The buyer receives goods and nothing else to do.
incoterms.watchOut: INDIA: a foreign supplier normally cannot be the importer of record without an Indian IEC and GST registration. "DDP" from an overseas supplier therefore usually means they pay a broker while the Bill of Entry is still filed in the Indian buyer's name — the duty is recorded against us and the IGST credit accrues to us, whoever actually funded it. Confirm who is on the Bill of Entry before treating the duty as somebody else's cost.

incoterms.name: Free On Road / Rail (Indian domestic convention)
incoterms.deliveryPoint: At the buyer's premises within India
incoterms.riskTransfersAt: On delivery at the buyer’s premises

carriage.note: Freight to our premises is inside the price.

insurance.note: Transit cover is usually the supplier’s, but it is a matter of contract, not of rule.

incoterms.implies: A domestic Indian term, not an Incoterm. Goods move within India, so there is no import: no Bill of Entry, no BCD, no SWS. GST is charged on the supplier's invoice and is creditable to us in the normal way.
incoterms.watchOut: Because it is not an Incoterm it has no agreed definition, so what "FOR" covers varies by supplier. Write the delivery point and who insures transit into the purchase order rather than relying on the abbreviation.
